--- title: "[Graph.invert_edge_selection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Invert edge selection (select unselected, unselect selected). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12667-L12728){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.invert_edge_selection() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Invert edge selection](/assets/graphs/invert-edge-selection.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: edges A–B, B–E, and E–F are selected in the accent color. After invert_edge_selection the selection flips: the other four edges are selected and those three are plain." width="100%"} Replaces the edge selection with its complement: every currently selected edge becomes unselected and every unselected edge becomes selected. With nothing selected, the result is that all edges are selected. This is the edge counterpart of `invert_node_selection()` and is handy for "keep only" operations -- select the edges to keep, invert, then `delete_edges_ws()` -- or for applying an attribute to every edge *except* a chosen few with `set_edge_attrs_ws()`. Only the edge selection is inverted; the node selection is left as is. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting one edge of a 5-edge cycle and inverting flips the selection to the remaining four: ::: {#632893fa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) first_edge = graph.get_edge_ids()[0] graph.select_edges_by_id([first_edge]).invert_edge_selection() graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: A "keep only" pattern: select the strong ties, invert so the weak ones are selected, and delete them. Only the two edges with weight of at least `0.5` survive: ::: {#8b82e5aa .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 0.9), ("B", "C", 0.2), ("C", "D", 0.7), ("D", "A", 0.1)]) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight >= 0.5) .invert_edge_selection() .delete_edges_ws() ) graph.get_edge_df().select("source", "target", "weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
